title: Ask a craving what it wants
line: Five days, three cravings a day, and the fullness each was after.
intro: Athena teaches that behind every desire the soul is seeking the fullness (κόρος) of the Good, so desire is sacred in its motive; it goes astray only when it believes that fullness lies in one more possession or one more meal. For five days you stop at three cravings a day and ask each what it really wants.
does: For five days, stop at three cravings a day and ask what fullness each is after.
trains: Hearing the longing for the Good behind ordinary desire.
each: When a craving pulls (a snack, a purchase, the phone, a drink, someone’s attention), pause before you act and ask: what fullness am I really after? Rest, company, recognition, comfort? Then look for a moment for that fullness within. You may still have the snack: the asking is the exercise. Note three cravings a day.
note: Your three cravings today, and the fullness each was after.
end: After five days, which fullness did your cravings seek most often, and where could you look for it directly?
